title: KnowledgeSettings
description: Data file content/knowledge/settings.json: how knowledge with its source behaves in the core (B4a R3, R4, R7, W1595): confidence by source, trust between inhabitants, which actions pass on what, what the routine leaves alone while a question is open, and how much goes to the decider. Values are placeholders (F5262: placeholders count as start values).

experienced_confidence.description: Confidence of what an inhabitant tried out itself (spec: certain).

guessed_cap.description: Highest confidence of an AI guess.

trust_true_heard_gain.description: Trust gained in a teller when one's own experience confirms what one heard.

trust_false_heard_loss.description: Trust lost in a teller when one's own experience contradicts what one heard.

min_teller_confidence.description: Only knowledge at least this sure is passed on.

wait_while_question_open.description: Actions the routine does not do on a thing while its question to the AI is out - sent and not yet answered (W1595, A1551). A question that only waits (held back, for the night, or for its next try after an error) holds nothing back: nobody is working on its answer.

request_max_knowledge.description: Most knowledge entries in one decider request (text budget). At most 32 (decision-request: knowledge holds 32).

request_max_inhabitants.description: Most perceived inhabitants and relationships in one decider request. At most 16 (decision-request: perception.inhabitants and relationships hold 16).

max_pass_on_options.description: Most options for passing knowledge on in one decision request (the request holds at most 32 options in all).

KnowledgeMemory.description: Memory (B4a R5, B7): the core keeps per inhabitant a summary and its remembered events. Which core events are remembered and which of them are formative is data (events). In the compute night the events not yet in the summary are condensed by the AI service (job memory) once there are condense_at of them; the core checks every answer itself. Without an AI service the events only pile up to max_events. Absent = nothing is remembered and the requests carry an empty memory. Values are placeholders.

condense_at.description: A compute night condenses an inhabitant's memory once at least this many of its entries are not in the summary yet (new since the last condensing, or sent with a job that failed). Small on purpose: the summary is what the decider, the questions and the conversation read as the story so far, so it should follow every night that brought something new.

job_max_events.description: Most events in one memory job, oldest first; more go into further jobs. At most 32 (generation-job: memory.events holds 32).

job_max_formative.description: Most formative events in one memory job (each must stay in the summary, so the text budget limits them); a job ends before the next one. At most job_max_events (checked at load).

max_chars.description: Text budget of the summary in characters (generation-job: memory.max_chars 100..1200).

max_events.description: Most remembered events per inhabitant. Beyond it the oldest event that is not formative is forgotten first, then the oldest formative one that is already in the summary, then the oldest. At least condense_at (checked at load).

job_priority.description: Priority of memory jobs (generation-job: higher runs first).

events.description: Which core events an inhabitant remembers. Every entry that fits an event gives one remembered event.

KnowledgeMemoryEvent.description: A core event the inhabitant it is about remembers: its kind in the memory, and whether it is formative (it must stay in the summary). What it is about follows from the event's target: another inhabitant, the object type of a thing, or nothing.

detail_ends_with.description: Only events whose language-neutral detail ends with this text (as in event_effects). Omitted = every event of the kind.

kind.description: Kind of the remembered event (a word the memory uses, e.g. felt_bad). Omitted = the event kind, or the action with action_as_kind.

action_as_kind.description: True = the action of the event is the kind of the remembered event (e.g. eat, drink); not together with kind. Omitted = false.

left_out_actions.description: Events of these actions are not remembered by this entry.

formative.description: never = an everyday event; first = formative the first time the inhabitant remembers this kind about this subject (with with_outcome: and with this outcome); always = formative every time.

with_outcome.description: True = the remembered event carries what came of the action (done, found_out, nothing; only finished actions have an outcome), so an attempt is not remembered as a deed. Each outcome then has its own first time and its own count. Omitted = false.

everyday_outcomes.description: Outcomes (done, found_out, nothing; checked at load) that are never formative for this entry, whatever formative says (e.g. nothing, if a first attempt without any effect should not shape). Omitted = none: the first time is formative with every outcome.

repeat.description: What a repetition does: add = every event is an entry of its own; counted = an event of the same kind (and outcome) about the same subject whose entry is still open (not yet sent to a condensing) is counted on that entry (times + 1, its tick becomes the last time, and it counts as the newest event) instead of added. A formative first time stays formative. Omitted = add.

both.description: True = an event aimed at another inhabitant is remembered by that inhabitant too, about the actor (e.g. first_meeting, which the core reports once per pair). Omitted = false.

only_with_subject.description: True = only events that are about something (another inhabitant or a thing); what the inhabitant did without a target (looking around, sleeping) is not remembered by this entry. Omitted = false.

KnowledgeMemoryEffect.description: Only events of an action that has such an effect on this target (the action's effects by the target's true properties, content/effects): how a meal that made sick or a drink that made thirstier becomes a memory of its own. The inhabitant remembers what it felt, never the property behind it.

id.description: Need or mood id; omitted = any need or mood; ignored for will_to_live.

delta_at_most.description: The effect's delta is at most this (e.g. -0.1 for a clear loss).

delta_at_least.description: The effect's delta is at least this (e.g. 0.2 for a clear gain).

KnowledgeNightQuestions.description: Questions in the compute night (B7, W1764): for every open question about an object type the core asks the AI service for a guess (job question), per inhabitant after its memory job. The guesses become beliefs with source guessed, at most as sure as guessed_cap, and never replace a belief the inhabitant already has; an answer that did not understand leaves the question open. Absent = no question jobs.

job_priority.description: Priority of question jobs (generation-job: higher runs first).

questions.description: Which open questions get a guess; a trigger that is not listed gets none.

KnowledgeNightQuestion.description: An open question of a trigger (decider settings) and what the inhabitant asks itself about the thing.

trigger.description: Trigger kind of the open question (decider-settings: triggers); only questions about an object type are asked.

question.description: Question kind of the job (generation-job: payload.question.question).

KnowledgeStartRelationships.description: Relationships of the start inhabitants when the world begins (B4a R8, F5249): members of the same start group know each other (partners), members of another group are strangers. Set for every pair at the start; absent = everybody starts with relationship_start.

partners.description: Towards a member of the own start group.

strangers.description: Towards a member of another start group (an unknown human; below the togetherness thresholds of the inhabitant model, checked at load).

KnowledgeRelationChange.description: A change of affection, trust and respect (each -1..1); the results stay within 0..1.

KnowledgeRelationAction.description: An action aimed at another inhabitant that, when it ends, changes how both see each other: the actor towards the listener and the listener towards the actor.

action.description: An action with an inhabitant target.

KnowledgeRelationshipChanges.description: How shared experiences change relationships between inhabitants (B4a R7): time spent near each other, actions towards each other, and heard knowledge that one's own experience proved right or wrong; closeness fades slowly towards fade_to. Only values above fade_to fade (a grudge or a stranger is not forgotten into acquaintance). Deterministic, every value is data. Absent = only trust changes (trust_true_heard_gain, trust_false_heard_loss).

together_distance_m.description: Two inhabitants within this distance spend time together.

together_per_hour.description: Change per hour spent together, for both.

heard_true.description: Change towards a teller when one's own experience confirms what one heard (on top of trust_true_heard_gain).

heard_false.description: Change towards a teller when one's own experience contradicts what one heard (on top of trust_false_heard_loss).

fade_per_hour.description: How much each value above fade_to sinks per hour (never below fade_to).

KnowledgeMeeting.description: Actions towards another inhabitant in sight that the core offers to the decider (B4a R8: observe, approach, trust, care grow from options and relationship values, not from a script). Each option is offered only while all of its conditions hold. Absent = none of these actions is offered.

KnowledgeMeetingOption.description: One action towards another inhabitant and when it is offered; omitted conditions always hold.

action.description: An action with an inhabitant target (not a passing or naming action).

min_distance_m.description: Only while the other is farther away than this.

max_trust.description: Only while the asker's trust in the other is below this.

max_affection.description: Only while the asker's affection for the other is below this.

need.description: A need of the asker that must be below need_below.

KnowledgeImprinting.description: Imprinting (B4a R6): the core only counts repeated experiences per inhabitant - a finished action, what it was about (object type or inhabitant; none for actions without a target) and the time of day. Each repetition adds one, every hour fades the counter a little; a counter from habit_from on is a habit, its strength the counter over full_at (at most 1). Habits are information for the decider only; the routine does not weigh them.

fade_per_hour.description: How much every counter sinks per hour.

habit_from.description: A counter at least this high is a habit.

full_at.description: Counter at which a habit has full strength 1; counters never grow above it (at least habit_from, checked at load).

forget_below.description: A counter that has faded below this is forgotten.

max_counters.description: Most counters per inhabitant; beyond it the weakest is forgotten (ties by key).

max_habits.description: Most habits in one decider request, strongest first (text budget). At most 8 (decision-request: habits holds 8).

KnowledgeRelationship.description: Values 0..1 towards someone one has just met.

KnowledgeNaming.description: Learning names on a first meeting (Marcel W1698): the action (inhabitant target) is offered only while the asker does not know the other's name; when it ends the other learns the asker's name, and the asker learns the other's unless the other is busy with an urgent need (a need below busy_need_below). Each learner gets the event name_learned. Absent = nobody learns names.

action.description: The action that introduces oneself (inhabitant target).

busy_need_below.description: The other answers with its own name only while none of its needs is below this level (0 = always answers).

KnowledgeLooking.description: What looking closely at a thing teaches (TL #19921): the properties one can see, guesses from them, and where the thing stands (place memory). Never the effect: a visible property must not be one an action's effect depends on (checked at load); whether something fills, poisons or quenches thirst is learned by trying, being told or an answered question. Absent = looking teaches nothing.

action.description: The action that looks at a thing (object target).

visible_properties.description: Properties one can see by looking (kind, look, material); learned true or false.

inspect_confidence.description: Confidence of what one has seen (below experienced_confidence, checked at load).

guessed_confidence.description: Confidence of a guess from what one has seen (source guessed; at most guessed_cap, checked at load).

guesses.description: What one guesses from a visible property (e.g. looks like fruit: could be edible). A guess never replaces a belief one already has.

place_memory_max.description: Most remembered places (thing, type, position, tick) per inhabitant; the oldest is forgotten first.

KnowledgeGuess.description: A guess from something seen: a thing with the seen property may have the guessed one.

KnowledgePassing.description: An action that passes on knowledge to another inhabitant: which beliefs it carries.

value.description: Only beliefs with this value (null = either).
